"""Temporary diagnostic for the exact 60-message demo slice."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter

from eval.dataset import split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.schemas import Action
from triage.sop.index import build_index


items = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)[:60]
index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()

scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]
classifications = classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs])

outcomes: Counter[str] = Counter()
predicted: Counter[str] = Counter()
low_confidences: list[float] = []
for scrub, classification in zip(scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    flags = detect_flags(scrub.text, classification)
    decision = route(
        score,
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        flags,
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    predicted[classification.label] += 1
    if decision.is_automated:
        outcomes[decision.action.value] += 1
    else:
        reason = decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
        outcomes[reason] += 1
        if reason == "low_confidence":
            low_confidences.append(decision.confidence)

print("outcomes", dict(outcomes))
print("automated_routes", outcomes[Action.AUTO_REPLY.value] + outcomes[Action.REDIRECT.value])

print("predicted_classes", dict(predicted))
print(
    "low_confidence_range",
    (round(min(low_confidences), 4), round(max(low_confidences), 4))
    if low_confidences
    else None,
)

"""Temporary diagnostic for the exact 60-message demo slice."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.schemas import Action
from triage.sop.index import build_index


items = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)[:60]
index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()

scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]
classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    stop = min(start + 8, len(scrubs))
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start:stop]])
    )
    print("classified", stop, flush=True)

outcomes: Counter[str] = Counter()
predicted: Counter[str] = Counter()
class_outcomes: Counter[tuple[str, str]] = Counter()
low_confidences: list[float] = []
for scrub, classification in zip(scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    flags = detect_flags(scrub.text, classification)
    decision = route(
        score,
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        flags,
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    predicted[classification.label] += 1
    if decision.is_automated:
        outcome = decision.action.value
        outcomes[outcome] += 1
    else:
        outcome = decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
        outcomes[outcome] += 1
        if outcome == "low_confidence":
            low_confidences.append(decision.confidence)
    class_outcomes[(classification.label, outcome)] += 1

print("outcomes", dict(outcomes))
print("automated_routes", outcomes[Action.AUTO_REPLY.value] + outcomes[Action.REDIRECT.value])
print("route_escalations", 60 - outcomes[Action.AUTO_REPLY.value] - outcomes[Action.REDIRECT.value])
print("predicted_classes", dict(predicted))
print(
    "class_outcomes",
    {f"{label} -> {outcome}": count for (label, outcome), count in class_outcomes.items()},
)
print(
    "low_confidence_range",
    (round(min(low_confidences), 4), round(max(low_confidences), 4))
    if low_confidences
    else None,
)

“Needs attention” currently combines policy escalations with drafting failures; it does not mean the classifier failed.

For the exact 60-email batch:

| Outcome | Emails |
|---|---:|
| High-consequence: 27 scam + 5 hardship | 32 |
| Below confidence threshold | 9 |
| Account-specific information required | 5 |
| No supporting SOP | 5 |
| Eligible automated redirects | 9 |

So 51 emails were deliberately routed to an officer. The system attempted drafts for the 9 automated redirects. If you saw only 4 drafts, 5 drafting attempts failed—typically an API/model/quota issue—and those five were safely returned to the attention queue:

`51 routing escalations + 5 draft failures = 56 needing attention`

The high rate is intentional: the configured system automates only 11.6% of the full test set at approximately 1% observed routing risk. Substantive answers require confidence ≥ 0.93, while high-consequence, account-specific, and unsupported messages are always escalated regardless of confidence.

There is also a demo-data problem: the app selects the newest 60 synthetic emails, producing an odd mix dominated by 27 scam reports, 17 out-of-scope messages, and no ordinary safe auto-replies.

My recommended next changes are:

- Replace “Needs attention” with separate metrics for “Policy escalations” and “Draft failures.”
- Show the drafting failure reason prominently—rate limit, API error, or timeout.
- Build a fixed, representative demo inbox containing a healthy mixture of safe drafting cases, redirects, and genuine escalations.
- Keep the safety thresholds unchanged; lowering them merely to produce more drafts would undermine the project’s risk guarantees.

"""Temporary diagnostic for the balanced 60-message demonstration inbox."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


rows = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
labels = sorted({item.label for item in rows})
groups = {
    label: sorted(
        (item for item in rows if item.label == label),
        key=lambda item: (
            item.account_specific or item.computation_requested,
            -item.email.received_at.timestamp(),
            item.email.id,
        ),
    )
    for label in labels
}
items = []
for round_index in range(6):
    items.extend(groups[label][round_index] for label in labels)
items.sort(key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)

index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()
scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]
classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start : start + 8]])
    )

outcomes: Counter[str] = Counter()
truths: Counter[str] = Counter(item.label for item in items)
for scrub, classification in zip(scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    flags = detect_flags(scrub.text, classification)
    decision = route(
        score,
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        flags,
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    outcome = (
        decision.action.value
        if decision.is_automated
        else decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
    )
    outcomes[outcome] += 1

print("truth_mix", dict(truths))
print("outcomes", dict(outcomes))
print("automated", outcomes["auto_reply"] + outcomes["redirect"])

"""Temporary local-only selector for a fixed outcome-balanced demo inbox."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


def round_robin(pool: list[Labelled], count: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    """Choose across true topics without exposing those labels to runtime."""
    groups: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for item in pool:
        groups[item.label].append(item)
    labels = sorted(groups)
    chosen: list[Labelled] = []
    index = 0
    while len(chosen) < count:
        added = False
        for label in labels:
            if index < len(groups[label]):
                chosen.append(groups[label][index])
                added = True
                if len(chosen) == count:
                    break
        if not added:
            break
        index += 1
    return chosen


items = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()

scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]
classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start : start + 8]])
    )
    if (start + 8) % 80 == 0:
        print("classified", min(start + 8, len(items)), flush=True)

pools: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
for item, scrub, classification in zip(items, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    flags = detect_flags(scrub.text, classification)
    decision = route(
        score,
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        flags,
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    outcome = (
        decision.action.value
        if decision.is_automated
        else decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
    )
    pools[outcome].append(item)

quotas = {
    "auto_reply": 8,
    "redirect": 4,
    "high_consequence": 10,
    "no_supporting_sop": 8,
    "low_confidence": 10,
    "account_specific_signal": 8,
    "computation_requested": 8,
    "foreign_income_signal": 4,
}

selected: list[Labelled] = []
for outcome, count in quotas.items():
    candidates = pools[outcome]
    if len(candidates) < count:
        raise RuntimeError(f"only {len(candidates)} candidates for {outcome}, need {count}")
    selected.extend(round_robin(candidates, count))

selected.sort(key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
print("pool_sizes", {key: len(value) for key, value in pools.items()})
print("truth_mix", dict(Counter(item.label for item in selected)))
print("ids")
print(json.dumps([item.email.id for item in selected], indent=2))

"""Temporary local-only selector for a fixed outcome-balanced demo inbox."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


def round_robin(pool: list[Labelled], count: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    """Choose across true topics without exposing those labels to runtime."""
    groups: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for item in pool:
        groups[item.label].append(item)
    labels = sorted(groups)
    chosen: list[Labelled] = []
    index = 0
    while len(chosen) < count:
        added = False
        for label in labels:
            if index < len(groups[label]):
                chosen.append(groups[label][index])
                added = True
                if len(chosen) == count:
                    break
        if not added:
            break
        index += 1
    return chosen


items = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()

scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]
classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start : start + 8]])
    )
    if (start + 8) % 80 == 0:
        print("classified", min(start + 8, len(items)), flush=True)

pools: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
for item, scrub, classification in zip(items, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    flags = detect_flags(scrub.text, classification)
    decision = route(
        score,
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        flags,
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    outcome = (
        decision.action.value
        if decision.is_automated
        else decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
    )
    pools[outcome].append(item)

quotas = {
    "auto_reply": 8,
    "redirect": 4,
    "high_consequence": 10,
    "no_supporting_sop": 8,
    "low_confidence": 10,
    "account_specific_signal": 8,
    "computation_requested": 8,
    "foreign_income_signal": 4,
}

selected: list[Labelled] = []
for outcome, count in quotas.items():
    candidates = pools[outcome]
    if len(candidates) < count:
        raise RuntimeError(f"only {len(candidates)} candidates for {outcome}, need {count}")
    selected.extend(round_robin(candidates, count))

selected.sort(key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
print("pool_sizes", {key: len(value) for key, value in pools.items()})
print("truth_mix", dict(Counter(item.label for item in selected)))
print("ids")
print(json.dumps([item.email.id for item in selected], indent=2))

+

+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

+from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
+from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
+from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
+from triage.sop.index import build_index
+
+
+def round_robin(pool: list[Labelled], count: int) -> list[Labelled]:
+    groups: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
+    for item in pool:
+        groups[item.label].append(item)
+    labels = sorted(groups)
+    chosen: list[Labelled] = []
+    index = 0
+    while len(chosen) < count:
+        added = False
+        for label in labels:
+            if index < len(groups[label]):
+                chosen.append(groups[label][index])
+                added = True
+                if len(chosen) == count:
+                    break
+        if not added:
+            break
+        index += 1
+    return chosen
+
+
+items = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
+index = build_index()
+scrubber = Scrubber()
+classifier = EncoderClassifier()

+    )
+    if (start + 8) % 160 == 0:
+        print("classified", min(start + 8, len(items)), flush=True)
+
+pools: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
+for item, scrub, classification in zip(items, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
+    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
+    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)

"""Temporary local-only selector for the 40-message automation-forward demo."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


def round_robin(pool: list[Labelled], count: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    groups: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for item in pool:
        groups[item.label].append(item)
    labels = sorted(groups)
    chosen: list[Labelled] = []
    index = 0
    while len(chosen) < count:
        added = False
        for label in labels:
            if index < len(groups[label]):
                chosen.append(groups[label][index])
                added = True
                if len(chosen) == count:
                    break
        if not added:
            break
        index += 1
    return chosen


items = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()
scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]

classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start : start + 8]])
    )
    if (start + 8) % 160 == 0:
        print("classified", min(start + 8, len(items)), flush=True)

pools: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
for item, scrub, classification in zip(items, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    decision = route(
        score,
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        detect_flags(scrub.text, classification),
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    outcome = (
        decision.action.value
        if decision.is_automated
        else decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
    )
    pools[outcome].append(item)

quotas = {
    "auto_reply": 16,
    "redirect": 8,
    "high_consequence": 4,
    "no_supporting_sop": 3,
    "low_confidence": 3,
    "account_specific_signal": 2,
    "computation_requested": 2,
    "foreign_income_signal": 2,
}

selected: list[Labelled] = []
for outcome, count in quotas.items():
    if len(pools[outcome]) < count:
        raise RuntimeError(f"only {len(pools[outcome])} candidates for {outcome}, need {count}")
    selected.extend(round_robin(pools[outcome], count))

selected.sort(key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
print("truth_mix", dict(Counter(item.label for item in selected)))
print(json.dumps([item.email.id for item in selected], indent=2))

"""Temporary local-only selector for the 40-message automation-forward demo."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


def round_robin(pool: list[Labelled], count: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    groups: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for item in pool:
        groups[item.label].append(item)
    labels = sorted(groups)
    chosen: list[Labelled] = []
    index = 0
    while len(chosen) < count:
        added = False
        for label in labels:
            if index < len(groups[label]):
                chosen.append(groups[label][index])
                added = True
                if len(chosen) == count:
                    break
        if not added:
            break
        index += 1
    return chosen


items = sorted(split("test"), key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()
scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]

classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start : start + 8]])
    )
    if (start + 8) % 160 == 0:
        print("classified", min(start + 8, len(items)), flush=True)

pools: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
for item, scrub, classification in zip(items, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    decision = route(
        score,
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        detect_flags(scrub.text, classification),
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    outcome = (
        decision.action.value
        if decision.is_automated
        else decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
    )
    pools[outcome].append(item)

quotas = {
    "auto_reply": 16,
    "redirect": 8,
    "high_consequence": 4,
    "no_supporting_sop": 3,
    "low_confidence": 3,
    "account_specific_signal": 2,
    "computation_requested": 2,
    "foreign_income_signal": 2,
}

selected: list[Labelled] = []
for outcome, count in quotas.items():
    if len(pools[outcome]) < count:
        raise RuntimeError(f"only {len(pools[outcome])} candidates for {outcome}, need {count}")
    selected.extend(round_robin(pools[outcome], count))

selected.sort(key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
print("truth_mix", dict(Counter(item.label for item in selected)))
print(json.dumps([item.email.id for item in selected], indent=2))

"""Temporary local-only selector for the 20-message focused demo."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


def round_robin(pool: list[Labelled], count: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    groups: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for item in pool:
        groups[item.label].append(item)
    labels = sorted(groups)
    chosen: list[Labelled] = []
    index = 0
    while len(chosen) < count:
        for label in labels:
            if index < len(groups[label]):
                chosen.append(groups[label][index])
                if len(chosen) == count:
                    return chosen
        index += 1
    return chosen


manifest = json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "demo_inbox.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
by_id = {item.email.id: item for item in split("test")}
items = [by_id[email_id] for email_id in manifest["email_ids"]]

index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()
scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]
classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start : start + 8]])
    )

pools: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
for item, scrub, classification in zip(items, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    decision = route(
        calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler),
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        detect_flags(scrub.text, classification),
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    outcome = (
        decision.action.value
        if decision.is_automated
        else decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
    )
    pools[outcome].append(item)

quotas = {
    "auto_reply": 8,
    "redirect": 4,
    "high_consequence": 2,
    "no_supporting_sop": 1,
    "low_confidence": 2,
    "account_specific_signal": 1,
    "computation_requested": 1,
    "foreign_income_signal": 1,
}
selected = [item for outcome, count in quotas.items() for item in round_robin(pools[outcome], count)]
selected.sort(key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
print(json.dumps([item.email.id for item in selected], indent=2))

"""Temporary local-only selector for the 20-message focused demo."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


def round_robin(pool: list[Labelled], count: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    groups: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for item in pool:
        groups[item.label].append(item)
    labels = sorted(groups)
    chosen: list[Labelled] = []
    index = 0
    while len(chosen) < count:
        for label in labels:
            if index < len(groups[label]):
                chosen.append(groups[label][index])
                if len(chosen) == count:
                    return chosen
        index += 1
    return chosen


manifest = json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "demo_inbox.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
by_id = {item.email.id: item for item in split("test")}
items = [by_id[email_id] for email_id in manifest["email_ids"]]

index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()
scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in items]
classifications = []
for start in range(0, len(scrubs), 8):
    classifications.extend(
        classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs[start : start + 8]])
    )

pools: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
for item, scrub, classification in zip(items, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, index.bucket)
    decision = route(
        calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler),
        index.sops_for(classification.label),
        detect_flags(scrub.text, classification),
        thresholds,
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
    )
    outcome = (
        decision.action.value
        if decision.is_automated
        else decision.reason.value if decision.reason is not None else "unknown"
    )
    pools[outcome].append(item)

quotas = {
    "auto_reply": 8,
    "redirect": 4,
    "high_consequence": 2,
    "no_supporting_sop": 1,
    "low_confidence": 2,
    "account_specific_signal": 1,
    "computation_requested": 1,
    "foreign_income_signal": 1,
}
selected = [item for outcome, count in quotas.items() for item in round_robin(pools[outcome], count)]
selected.sort(key=lambda item: item.email.received_at, reverse=True)
print(json.dumps([item.email.id for item in selected], indent=2))

"""Load the frozen corpus and its splits.

EVAL-TIME and BUILD-TIME.

``Email`` forbids extra fields on purpose: an inbox message carries an id, a
timestamp, a sender, a subject and a body, and nothing else. A real inbound email
has no ``label``. The generated corpus carries both the message and the ground
truth the generator recorded, so this module is the seam that splits them --
:class:`Labelled` keeps the truth beside the email rather than smuggling it inside,
which is what stops a metric from ever reading a field the runtime cannot see.

The ground-truth fields exist because generation recorded them, not because they
were annotated afterwards: the scenario spec knows which class it wrote from, which
SOPs it drew on, and whether it planted a computation request or PII. That is what
makes flag precision/recall and grounding accuracy free to compute (``BUILD.md``
S5.2, S9.2).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Final

from triage.schemas import Email

#: Repository root, from this file.
ROOT: Final[Path] = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

DEFAULT_EMAILS: Final[Path] = ROOT / "data" / "generated" / "emails.jsonl"
DEFAULT_SPLITS: Final[Path] = ROOT / "data" / "splits" / "splits.json"

#: Keys belonging to the inbox message. Everything else in a row is ground truth.
_EMAIL_KEYS: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({
    "id", "received_at", "from", "subject", "body",
})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Labelled:
    """One generated email, with the ground truth recorded when it was written."""

    email: Email
    label: str
    scenario_id: str = ""
    source_sops: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    computation_requested: bool = False
    account_specific: bool = False
    plant_pii: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    season: str = ""
    persona_role: str = ""
    literacy: str = ""
    register: str = ""
    generator_model: str = ""

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        return self.email.id


def _row_to_labelled(row: dict[str, Any]) -> Labelled:
    return Labelled(
        email=Email.model_validate({k: v for k, v in row.items() if k in _EMAIL_KEYS}),
        label=str(row["label"]),
        scenario_id=str(row.get("scenario_id", "")),
        source_sops=tuple(row.get("source_sops") or ()),
        computation_requested=bool(row.get("computation_requested", False)),
        account_specific=bool(row.get("account_specific", False)),
        plant_pii=dict(row.get("plant_pii") or {}),
        season=str(row.get("season", "")),
        persona_role=str(row.get("persona_role", "")),
        literacy=str(row.get("literacy", "")),
        register=str(row.get("register", "")),
        generator_model=str(row.get("generator_model", "")),
    )


def load_emails(path: Path | None = None) -> tuple[Labelled, ...]:
    """Read ``emails.jsonl`` into labelled records."""
    source = path or DEFAULT_EMAILS
    if not source.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"no corpus at {source}. Run: python scripts/generate_emails.py"
        )
    with source.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return tuple(_row_to_labelled(json.loads(line)) for line in handle if line.strip())


def load_splits(path: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read the frozen split assignment: email id -> ``train``/``calibration``/``test``."""
    source = path or DEFAULT_SPLITS
    if not source.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"no splits at {source}. Run: python scripts/make_splits.py"
        )
    return dict(json.loads(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["assignment"])


def split(
    name: str,
    emails: tuple[Labelled, ...] | None = None,
    assignment: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[Labelled, ...]:
    """Return one split.

    Results are reported on ``test`` and never on ``calibration``: the temperature
    is fitted on the latter, so reporting there would be reporting on training data
    for the very quantity being measured (``BUILD.md`` S5.5).
    """
    rows = emails if emails is not None else load_emails()
    mapping = assignment if assignment is not None else load_splits()
    return tuple(row for row in rows if mapping.get(row.id) == name)


def iter_splits(
    emails: tuple[Labelled, ...] | None = None,
) -> Iterator[tuple[str, tuple[Labelled, ...]]]:
    """Yield each split by name, in pipeline order."""
    rows = emails if emails is not None else load_emails()
    mapping = load_splits()
    for name in ("train", "calibration", "test"):
        yield name, split(name, rows, mapping)

a metric. Six values, closed.

    consult the classifier's confidence and would fire identically at probability

    NO_SUPPORTING_SOP = "no_supporting_sop"
    COMPUTATION_REQUESTED = "computation_requested"
    ACCOUNT_SPECIFIC_SIGNAL = "account_specific_signal"

"""The router -- the single gate where escalation happens.

RUNTIME. The highest-value component in the system, and the one the tests cover
most heavily.

Escalation is one decision made in one place, after the SOP lookup and before
drafting. Everything upstream only produces evidence; nothing else in the pipeline
decides whether a citizen gets an automated reply.

Eight reasons, checked in this order:

===  ==============================  ============================
 #   reason                          consults confidence?
===  ==============================  ============================
 1   requires_account_lookup         no
 2   high_consequence                no
 3   no_supporting_sop               no
 4   computation_requested           no
 5   account_specific_signal         no
 6   foreign_income_signal           no
 7   scam_signal                     no
 8   low_confidence                  yes
===  ==============================  ============================

Only the last reads the model. The other seven are structural and would fire
identically at probability 1.0 -- which is what makes "these buckets always
escalate" a property that can be tested rather than hoped for.

Reasons 4-7 are flags, and each fires only where a SOP declares its trigger, so
the corpus decides which conditions matter for which procedure. Reasons 6 and 7
are MISFILE guards specifically: they exist for the case where the classifier put
an email in the wrong class, in the direction where that error is unsafe.

**Thresholds are per bucket, not per class.** Three of five buckets escalate
regardless of confidence, so only ``auto_answerable`` and ``out_of_scope`` have a
threshold that bites. The bucket is the level that determines the action and is
therefore the level where an operator sets policy (``sop_design.md`` S3).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Final

import yaml

from triage.schemas import (
    Action,
    Bucket,
    BucketScore,
    EscalationReason,
    Flag,
    RoutingDecision,
)
from triage.sop.loader import SOP

#: Bucket -> escalation reason, for the three that always escalate.
_BUCKET_REASON: Final[dict[Bucket, EscalationReason]] = {
    Bucket.REQUIRES_ACCOUNT_LOOKUP: EscalationReason.REQUIRES_ACCOUNT_LOOKUP,
    Bucket.HIGH_CONSEQUENCE: EscalationReason.HIGH_CONSEQUENCE,
    Bucket.NO_SUPPORTING_SOP: EscalationReason.NO_SUPPORTING_SOP,
}

#: Flag -> the reason it escalates under, and the frontmatter trigger a SOP must
#: declare for it to apply. The corpus decides which conditions matter for which
#: procedure; this map only says what each one is called.
_FLAG_REASON: Final[dict[Flag, tuple[EscalationReason, str]]] = {
    Flag.COMPUTATION_REQUESTED: (
        EscalationReason.COMPUTATION_REQUESTED, "computation_requested",
    ),
    Flag.ACCOUNT_SPECIFIC_SIGNAL: (
        EscalationReason.ACCOUNT_SPECIFIC_SIGNAL, "account_specific",
    ),
    # Two misfile guards. Each fires only where a SOP declares the trigger, so
    # they cost nothing on the classes that never asked for them: SOP-RES-001
    # declares `foreign_income_dta` and SOP-RTE-002 declares `scam_report`, which
    # is the corpus saying "if this email is really that, I must not answer it."
    Flag.FOREIGN_INCOME_SIGNAL: (
        EscalationReason.FOREIGN_INCOME_SIGNAL, "foreign_income_dta",
    ),
    Flag.SCAM_SIGNAL: (
        EscalationReason.SCAM_SIGNAL, "scam_report",
    ),
}

#: Used until calibration is fitted. A number produced under it must never be
#: reported (``BUILD.md`` S7); ``RoutingDecision.calibrated`` carries the
#: distinction so a placeholder cannot be mistaken for a result.
PLACEHOLDER_THRESHOLD: Final[float] = 0.5


def load_thresholds(path: str | None = None) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Read per-bucket thresholds from ``config/thresholds.yaml``.

    In config rather than code so the escalation policy is readable in one file,
    diffable in git, and changeable without touching the pipeline.
    """
    from pathlib import Path

    config = Path(path) if path else (
        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "config" / "thresholds.yaml"
    )
    if not config.exists():
        return dict.fromkeys(
            (b.value for b in Bucket), PLACEHOLDER_THRESHOLD,
        )
    doc = yaml.safe_load(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    return {
        bucket: float(entry["threshold"])
        for bucket, entry in (doc.get("buckets") or {}).items()
    }


def route(
    score: BucketScore,
    sops: tuple[SOP, ...],
    flags: frozenset[Flag],
    thresholds: dict[str, float],
    *,
    calibrated: bool = False,
    multiplier: float = 1.0,
) -> RoutingDecision:
    """Decide whether to act on this email, or hand it to an officer.

    Args:
        score: The rolled-up bucket and its confidence.
        sops: What the SOP lookup returned. Empty means unanswerable.
        flags: Orthogonal signals detected after the rollup.
        thresholds: Per-bucket cutoffs.
        calibrated: Whether ``score`` came from a fitted temperature.
        multiplier: Scales every threshold. Sweeping this generates the
            risk-coverage curve, so the curve is produced by the real router

"""Temporary selector audit for privacy-focused demo messages."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
manifest = json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "demo_inbox.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
current_ids = set(manifest["email_ids"])
rows = split("test")
candidates = [
    item
    for item in rows
    if item.id in current_ids or {"nric", "address"}.intersection(item.plant_pii)
]

index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()
bucket_of = dict(index.bucket)

scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in candidates]
classifications = classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs])

records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
for item, scrub, classification in zip(candidates, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, bucket_of)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    flags = detect_flags(scrub.text, classification)
    sops = index.sops_for(classification.label)
    decision = route(
        score,
        sops,
        flags,
        dict(thresholds),
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
        multiplier=1.0,
    )
    records.append(
        {
            "id": item.id,
            "current": item.id in current_ids,
            "pii": sorted(item.plant_pii),
            "money": re.findall(r"(?:S?\$\s?[\d,.]+(?:k|m)?|\b\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?\s+dollars?\b)", item.email.text, re.I),
            "action": decision.action.value,
            "reason": decision.reason.value if decision.reason else None,
            "predicted": classification.label,
            "subject": item.email.subject,
        }
    )

print("CURRENT")
for record in records:
    if record["current"]:
        print(json.dumps(record))

print("PRIVACY CANDIDATES")
for record in records:
    if record["pii"]:
        print(json.dumps(record))

item.stdout:
# PII detection patterns for the scrub node.
#
# Patterns live here rather than in code so the detection surface is readable in
# one file, diffable in git, and extensible without touching src/. Each entry
# carries a `justification:` recording why the pattern is drawn where it is â€”
# these are defended in the writeup, not just executed.
#
# Ordering matters. Patterns are applied top to bottom, and an earlier match
# consumes the span. Three orderings are load-bearing:
#
#   nric      before phone   â€” the seven digits inside an identifier are not a
#                              phone number
#   money     before postal  â€” a six-digit run carrying a currency marker is an
#                              amount, not a postal code, and matching postal
#                              first would strand the "$" outside the placeholder
#   postal_code_bare last    â€” an unanchored six-digit run is the weakest signal
#                              in the set, so every stronger pattern claims its
#                              span first

patterns:
  - name: nric
    placeholder: NRIC
    regex: '\b[STFGMstfgm]\d{7}[A-Za-z]\b'
    validator: nric_checksum
    justification: >
      The most sensitive identifier in scope. A checksum validator gates the
      match, so tokens of the same shape that are not identifiers (order
      references, case numbers) are left alone. Case-insensitive because
      citizens type these in lower case.

  - name: email
    placeholder: EMAIL
    regex: '\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b'
    justification: >
      Applied before phone and postal code. An address can contain digit runs
      that would otherwise be consumed by the numeric patterns.

  - name: phone_sg
    placeholder: PHONE
    regex: '(?<![\d-])(?:\+65[\s-]?)?[689]\d{3}[\s-]?\d{4}(?![\d-])'
    justification: >
      Singapore mobile and landline numbers are eight digits opening with 6, 8
      or 9. The optional +65 prefix and internal space or hyphen cover the
      common written forms. Lookarounds prevent matching inside a longer digit
      run such as an account number.

  - name: money
    placeholder: AMOUNT
    regex: '(?i)(?:S?\$\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?|\b\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?\s*(?:SGD|dollars?|bucks)\b|\bSGD\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?)'
    justification: >
      Assessed income and tax payable are financial facts about an individual.
      Runs BEFORE the postal patterns: a currency marker ($ or a currency word)
      disambiguates a six-digit run that would otherwise be read as a postal
      code, and matching postal first would strand the marker outside the
      placeholder. Any digit length is accepted, since incomes are not
      six-digit by nature.

  - name: postal_code_sg
    placeholder: POSTAL
    regex: '(?i)(?:\bS(?:INGAPORE)?\b[\s(]*|\bpost(?:al)?\s*code\s*:?\s*|\bpostal\s*:?\s*|\bs\(\s*)(?<!\d)\d{6}(?!\d)'
    justification: >
      Context-anchored postal codes: a Singapore or postal-code marker
      immediately precedes the digits. This is the high-precision form and
      carries no ambiguity with monetary or reference values.

      The marker alternation covers "postcode", "post code" and "postal code"
      as well as bare "postal". The one-word spelling was missing and is the
      one the generated corpus actually uses, so nine of sixteen planted
      postcodes were reachable only by the bare pattern -- which was itself
      rejecting them (see postal_code_bare).

  - name: block_street_unit
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:blk|block)\s*\d{1,4}[A-Z]?\b(?:\s+(?:(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+\s+){1,3}(?:AVENUE|AVE|ROAD|RD|CRESCENT|CLOSE|WALK|RISE|DRIVE|LINK|STREET|ST|LANE|PLACE|TERRACE|VIEW|GARDENS?|PARK|HEIGHTS|WAY)\b(?:\s+\d{1,3})?|(?:JALAN|LORONG|BUKIT|TAMAN)\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+(?:\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+){0,2}))?(?:\s*#\s*\d{1,3}\s*-\s*\d{1,4})?'
    justification: >
      A full HDB address claimed as ONE span: block, street and unit together.
      Runs BEFORE block_unit, and that ordering is load-bearing. block_unit
      matches only "Blk 857" and consumes the span, which left the street name
      ("Tampines Street 21") stranded between two placeholders with no pattern
      able to reach it -- the leading house number that street_address requires
      had already been taken. Every planted address in the corpus is this shape,
      so the leak was total for the address type while scrub recall still read
      1.0000: the metric asks whether the WHOLE planted string survives verbatim,
      and a partly-scrubbed address does not.

      The street segment is optional, so this pattern strictly supersedes
      block_unit rather than competing with it. Its two branches are ordered
      trailing-type first: "Bukit Batok Ave 3" carries both a leading type
      (Bukit) and a trailing one (Ave), and the leading branch would stop at
      "Bukit Batok" and strand "Ave 3".

      Deliberately anchored on the block token. A standalone street pattern was
      prototyped and rejected: the gazetteer's English members (WAY, LINK, VIEW,
      PLACE, ST) are ordinary words, and it fired on 80+ non-address phrases
      across the corpus ("is there any way", "clicked the link"), scrubbing the
      topical text the classifier reads. Anchored on the block it matches 16
      spans corpus-wide, all 16 of them planted addresses, zero false positives.

  - name: block_unit
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:blk|block)\s*\d{1,4}[A-Z]?\b(?:\s*#\s*\d{1,3}\s*-\s*\d{1,4})?'
    justification: >
      HDB block and unit numbers. The unit portion is optional because a block
      number alone is still locating information.

  - name: unit_number
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '#\s*\d{1,3}\s*-\s*\d{1,4}\b'
    justification: >
      A bare unit number appearing without its block, which the block_unit
      pattern would not reach.

  - name: street_address
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b\d{1,4}[A-Z]?\s+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+\s+){0,3}(?:JALAN|LORONG|BUKIT|TAMAN|AVENUE|AVE|ROAD|RD|CRESCENT|CLOSE|WALK|RISE|DRIVE|LINK|STREET|ST|LANE|PLACE|TERRACE|VIEW|GARDENS?|PARK|HEIGHTS)\b'
    justification: >
      Gazetteer-anchored street matching. A street-type token is required, so
      the pattern cannot fire on arbitrary capitalised text. Named-but-untyped
      streets are the known residual gap and are reported as such rather than
      claimed covered.

  - name: street_address_prefixed
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:JALAN|LORONG|BUKIT|TAMAN)\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+(?:\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+){0,2}'
    justification: >
      Malay street types lead rather than trail the name (Jalan Besar, Bukit
      Timah), so they need a separate pattern from the trailing-type form.

  - name: date
    placeholder: DATE
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{2,4}|\d{1,2}\s+(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\.?\s+\d{4})\b'
    justification: >
      Dates of birth and specific transaction dates are identifying in
      combination. Bare years are excluded: a Year of Assessment is topical
      content the classifier needs, not PII.

  - name: postal_code_bare
    placeholder: POSTAL
    regex: '(?<![\d.,$])\d{6}(?![\d.,]?\d)'
    justification: >
      A bare six-digit run with no currency marker and no postal keyword. Kept
      deliberately broad because over-scrubbing is the correct failure
      direction for an identifier that localises a residence, but it runs after
      money and after the context-anchored form, so amounts and marked postal
      codes are already claimed. The residual false-positive class is
      unmarked six-digit reference numbers, which is reported rather than
      claimed fixed. The lookarounds exclude decimals and thousands-separated
      numbers so a fragment of a larger figure is never matched.

      The trailing lookahead is (?![\d.,]?\d) rather than (?![\d.,]). Its job is
      to reject a six-digit run that CONTINUES into a larger number -- a decimal
      or a thousands-separated figure -- so what disqualifies a match is a
      separator FOLLOWED BY ANOTHER DIGIT. The earlier form rejected any
      trailing "." or ",", which meant an ordinary sentence-ending postcode
      ("postcode 648913.") was skipped while the same value written with a "?"
      was caught. That asymmetry silently dropped nine of sixteen planted
      postcodes.

# Tokens that must never be scrubbed even where a pattern would match them.
# These are topical vocabulary the classifier depends on.
allowlist:
  - '(?i)\bYA\s?20\d{2}\b'
  - '(?i)\byear of assessment\b'
  - '(?i)\bIRAS\b'
  - '(?i)\bmyTax\s?Portal\b'

"""Temporary selector audit for privacy-focused demo messages."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split
from triage.models.calibration import TemperatureScaler
from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier
from triage.nodes.calibrate import calibrate, rollup
from triage.nodes.flags import detect_flags
from triage.nodes.route import load_thresholds, route
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber
from triage.sop.index import build_index


manifest = json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "demo_inbox.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
current_ids = set(manifest["email_ids"])
rows = split("test")
candidates = [
    item
    for item in rows
    if item.id in current_ids or {"nric", "address"}.intersection(item.plant_pii)
]

index = build_index()
scrubber = Scrubber()
classifier = EncoderClassifier()
scaler = TemperatureScaler.load()
thresholds = load_thresholds()
bucket_of = dict(index.bucket)

scrubs = [scrubber.scrub(item.email.text) for item in candidates]
classifications = classifier.predict_batch([scrub.text for scrub in scrubs])

records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
for item, scrub, classification in zip(candidates, scrubs, classifications, strict=True):
    bucket, summed = rollup(classification, bucket_of)
    score = calibrate(bucket, summed, scaler)
    flags = detect_flags(scrub.text, classification)
    sops = index.sops_for(classification.label)
    decision = route(
        score,
        sops,
        flags,
        dict(thresholds),
        calibrated=scaler.fitted,
        multiplier=1.0,
    )
    records.append(
        {
            "id": item.id,
            "current": item.id in current_ids,
            "pii": sorted(item.plant_pii),
            "money": re.findall(r"(?:S?\$\s?[\d,.]+(?:k|m)?|\b\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?\s+dollars?\b)", item.email.text, re.I),
            "action": decision.action.value,
            "reason": decision.reason.value if decision.reason else None,
            "predicted": classification.label,
            "subject": item.email.subject,
        }
    )

print("CURRENT")
for record in records:
    if record["current"]:
        print(json.dumps(record))

print("PRIVACY CANDIDATES")
for record in records:
    if record["pii"]:
        print(json.dumps(record))
